8.t: Learning to bow from Nicholson and Henry Kimball
8.s: Gut strings, learning by watching Sam Nicholson and Danny Lewis, then Henry Kimball showing him fingering and bowing and the E-string.
8.q: I'd go around different places like I'd go around where the Eagle Band was playing. Danny Lewis would be playing, you know.

8.t: Bowing lessons from Wallace, president of Local 47
8.s: Wallace, a trombone and bass man who played with Whiteman, teaches him bowing but Garland insists on his own jazz bass approach.
8.q: And I quit that. So I really got onto wanting to bow. I went to -- I don't know if I can recall this man's name. He used to play a trombone and he played bass, with Paul Whiteman. His name was --

8.t: Learning to read and bass lessons
8.s: He faked at first, got some reading from Dave Jackson, and got ideas and fingerboard instruction from older bassists.
8.q: Yeah, I started out with faking, yeah. A little reading I'd done, a little learning I got. I started at Dave, at Old Man Jackson. Yeah.

874.t: Simon Marrero teaches him to bow and repair bass
874.s: Simon Marrero taught him to read and bow, and he practically lived at Marrero's house. He started in his teens.
874.q: Jimmy Johnson, yes. Mr. Johnson. I always called him Mr. Johnson. As a bass player. Yes, he was another one. He played up now mostly. Yeah. He was a fine bass player too. Yes, he did. All those men used to read very good. They were good readers. Like old man Kimball and Jimmy. And this fellow, I'm…

874.t: Bass method and studying the hard way
874.s: He describes starting on a four-string bass and studying with Marrero's method book, with little other teaching.
874.q: No. No. But I could play three strings. I started with four. Simon Morrill was one. That's the first thing he told me, he said, you've got to play the right type of bass. You've got to learn to play the E strings. They're all played. He just wanted to think, it's note on all strings. So I started…

1024.t: Teaching himself bass from a book
1024.ch: Learning bass and Dew Drop days
1024.q: Yeah, well after I, see I never took bass at Greenwald School. Yeah, mostly self-taught there, you know. So what happened, after I finished that gig with Montra, Texas Lodge, I went on the road. But I didn't go out there playing bass. I went out there playing piano with Clyde and them, you know.…

38.s: Levy teaches students sent by Professor Dyett and Jimmy Noone, including Noone's nephew Henry, and they compare bassists named Henry Ford.
38.q: I had some kids from school. I lived around the corner from DuSable High School. And I had some kids that Professor Dyett sent me. He knew that I would teach them very good fundamentals. And I had some violin students. I had some bander students too. In fact, I taught Jimmy Noon's nephew. Henry.…

817.t: Picking, never bowing, and no formal lessons
817.s: He only picked the bass, never mastered the bow, and Tasso's attempts to teach him music failed.
817.q: No, Mr. Tasso tried to teach me but I never could get my heart to learn the music, you know. I just wanted to play music and play jazz and that was about it, you know.

972.t: Building his first bass from a soapbox and barrel
972.s: He recounts making a bass from a soapbox with twine, marking strings in pencil, getting a tuning key, and later building one from a barrel.
972.q: Yeah, yeah. So give me a D string. He said, I have a D string. I'm like, I put D. I use G. I put G. I use G. So, he said, I have G. I eat. I eat. Uh-huh. That's all I want, you know. And I thought I'd go to dance. Well, like, on a Monday, it was a Blue Monday. Well, Raps and Slane, they call me,…

828.s: Humphrey would help students with popular music if they brought parts, and urged an instrument with more work.
828.q: That's why he told me I was wasting my time fooling with a violin. He wanted me to get on an instrument that I could get out of. I played several jobs from Tronc Wonder with my father-in-law and others. I played Daphonis with him. This fellow here where I'm playing the bass horn, where I play the…

282.t: Learning string bass and other string instruments by ear
282.s: He learned the tuba first, then picked up string bass from his violin, guitar and mandolin background, not by reading music.
282.q: I used to play the ghetto. Jim had a ghetto and I'd learn on that. And the mandolin, I'd learn on that, you see. Well, that made me play the little fiddle by head, the drum, no I mean the ghetto by head, and the mandolin.

877.t: Learning bass with no teacher; Selby Thomas's violin
877.s: Handy had no teacher; his father's band rehearsed, and bassist Selby Thomas had a fine oversized bass that Handy learned on.
877.q: My father had a band. Just like we would be here. And he would call a rehearsal. And they called a rehearsal. And the fellow was named Selby Thomas.

248.t: Taking up string bass and tenor banjo
248.s: Hired as bass player by Manuel Perez's Imperial band after Billy Moran left; self-taught on bass, about ten years on tenor banjo.
248.q: Tenor band, yeah. When did you take up the bass? I had taken up the bass after I put the tenor band on. I had taken up the bass. They hired me, what you call, Emmanuel Perez, them. They had some misunderstanding with Billy Moran, the bass player. Yes. And they led Billy Moran. It was Imperial Band.…

339.t: Teaching himself the bass from a Bob Haggart book
339.s: Told the club wants a bass, he buys one, learns from a book and plays everything on one string; ukulele helped his tone and chords.
339.q: On ukulele. At the end of the year he says, “everybody keeps asking about a bass fiddle.” He said, “You don’t have one of these.” So I said uh oh, they’re going to get rid of me and get a bass. So what I did, I went down the next day to a place and got me a bass. I brought it home, didn’t know…

70.t: Learning bass and tuba fingering from Billy Taylor
70.s: Watching Billy Taylor, he finds bass fingers like violin and works out how tuba valves correspond to trombone positions.
70.q: -- so I used to fool with Billy's bass and then he had a tuba. Well, then I got to fooling with this tuba, too, and I found it dawned on me that the B-flat instruments were all relative. All the notes he made open on the tuba I could make closed on the first position on the trombone, you see.

170.t: Bassists who helped him: Truck Parham and others
170.s: Truck Parham shows him double stops and other bassists give him strings.
170.q: No. I had some -- there was a bass player named Truck Parham - saw me out on the street, you know, with my fiddle, he said, "Come by the house" -- and I went by his house one day; you know, I didn't have no money to pay him but he wanted to help me -- a young kid, you know -- and he showed me how…

171.t: Learning bass from a Frank Skinner chart
171.s: He taught himself using a chart pasted on his bass, despite his double-jointed fingers.
171.q: Yeah. And I value that better than any -- I didn't have too much real music training, teaching, anyway. Because I bought a chart, it was a Frank Skinner book, and in the middle of that book was a chart to paste on a bass fiddle. When I first got that bass fiddle I got that chart and I pasted it on…
